A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Counterfactual Identifiability via Dynamic Optimal Transport. Their complete main text, Appendices A–F, equations, 12 tables and 15 figures support reliable comparison. An additional reference page shifts appendix pagination in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original counterfactual ellipse experiments and MIMIC-CXR evaluations, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and generated examples in Section 6 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original ellipse and MIMIC-CXR results, including the quantitative evaluations and qualitative examples in Section 6 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The EBM, FLOW, OT-EBM and OT-FLOW variants, conditional Markovian Batch-OT coupling, training objectives and ODE-based counterfactual inference remain unchanged. The wording edits introduce no procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the Markovian and frontdoor ellipse experiments, prior-complexity and assumption-violation scenarios, and MIMIC-CXR evaluations involving sex, race, age and pleural effusion. No evaluated dataset or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the Nasr-Esfahany et al. (2023) ellipse baselines, NAIVE OT coupling, and Ribeiro et al. (2023)/Xia et al. (2024) chest X-ray baselines. The newly cited works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The data partitions, training budgets, model sizes, metrics, solver settings and age-bin experiments are unchanged. For example, both retain the 70/10/20 ellipse split and the 192×192 MIMIC-CXR setup with a 22M-parameter model and batch size 64.

E4.justification: Both retain the prior-complexity, monotonicity, bijectivity and Markovianity ablations in Tables 3–6, the OT and age-bin studies in Tables 10–12, and the curl, reversibility and direct-effect visual analyses. Figure 4 restyles existing examples.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting remains unchanged, including the ± entries, three random-seed runs documented in Appendix F.2, and three randomly seeded subsets of 1,000 test samples in Table 9. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains 0.76 ± 0.01% error for Markovian OT-FLOW at 50 function evaluations. Figure 4 contains the same 24 X-ray images.

T1.justification: The definitions, formal assumptions, theorems and proofs remain unchanged, including frontdoor Lemma B.13 and its proof. The local Section 5 scope edit does not revise that formal result; removing redundant parentheses in Equation 15 is mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph and conclusion retain the same claims about multivariate counterfactual identification through continuous flows and dynamic OT, non-Markovian extensions, and empirical counterfactual soundness. The introductory rewrite does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 changes “BC/FC” to “BC” when summarising sufficiency of bijectivity plus variability and prescribing standard flows. This narrows the local applicability guidance, but Section 4.3, Lemma B.13 and the frontdoor experiments remain. Other interpretations and limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The dataset construction instructions, architectures, hyperparameters, training and model-selection procedures, and L40 hardware disclosure remain unchanged in Appendices E–F. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mehta et al. (2025), CF-Seg, to the introduction and De Sousa Ribeiro and Glocker (2025) and Balcerak et al. (2025) to Remark C.2's energy-based-model discussion. These are limited citation additions without substantial repositioning.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites one introductory paragraph, makes scattered spelling, grammar and punctuation corrections, and adds acknowledgments to Aapo Hyvärinen and Charles Jones. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 replaces “Observation” with “Factual” and uses bold, colored row labels while retaining its images and intervention annotations. Other visual changes are limited to text and bibliography reflow; tables and remaining figures retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 adds light editorial polish, supporting citations and clearer Figure 4 labels. Its formal arguments, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, while the isolated Section 5 wording edit leaves the frontdoor result intact elsewhere. These limited changes leave the paper's overall evidential strength and assessability essentially unchanged.
